newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Mackie to reduce dependence on textile machinery.
newsitem.headline: Mackie to reduce dependence on textile machinery.

text.p: Northern Irish-based engineering group Mackie International Group Plc said on Wednesday that the group's dependence on its textile machinery business would be reduced further in 1997.
Reduced world-wide demand for linen resulted in an extremely difficult trading period for the textile machinery operations last year, Mackie said.

This, together with a 1.9 million sterling exceptional charge relating to the restructuring of the textile operations and pension provisions, resulted in a pre-tax loss of 0.44 million sterling in 1996, the group said in its annual results statement.
Mackie said the outlook for the textile machinery business remains difficult.
"However, there are signs that the demand for linen may have begun to rise and that augurs well for some of the major investment programmes which demand Mackie equipment."
Mackie said the outlook for its new businesses was good.
The company's non-textile businesses achieved sales of 6.1 million sterling against 3.4 million a year earlier and now represent 65 percent of group turnover.
"Further significant increases are expected in 1997 and beyond," Mackie said.
It said there was strong interest from European customers in its Springvale foundry which is currently under construction and which will start production on the first new line at the end of April.

Mackie's joint venture with Meshmaster Inc to produce processing machinery to manufacture steel reinforcing mesh has had an excellent entry into its market and orders are already in place with further progress anticipated, the group said.
Mackie Environmental has also won major business. It is expected to double its 1996 turnover this year and already has contracts to cover most of this increase.

"We will continue to develop these growth businesses and seek to expand the base of Mackie with appropriate acquisitions. In this way, textile machinery will become part of a family of engineering operations and its pre-eminent position in its sector can be more fully and profitably exploited," Mackie said.
The company, which is actively reviewing appropriate acquisition opportunities, said its financial position remained strong with net assets of 23.6 million sterling and net borrowings of 1.5 million.
Mackie also announced the appointment of Sul Sahota, who was formerly business development director of Burnfield Plc, as its new chief executive.
Peter Long, the former CEO, has resigned to pursue other interests while executive chairman Patrick Dougan will also step down and Roger Looker will resume the role of chairman, the company said.
